subjects.term: MSC2020 52B05: Combinatorial properties of polytopes and polyhedra

title: Scutoid Tissues in Four Dimensions
description:
Version 3 adds references (the 600-cell family: Coxeter; Conway and Guy; Conway, Burgiel and Goodman-Strauss; DICTO #63, #65, #76; and the scutoid follow-ups that count exchanges, Gómez-Gálvez et al. 2021, 2022) and a credited gallery search for the figures. No result changes.

Version 2 adds, after an external review: terminology, Theorem 1′ for d ≥ 4 with the index table, classical and new marked, the g-theorem in tissue terms, the four-layer condition defined, a Verification section for the computer-assisted proof of Theorem 3 (re-run from a clean checkout with identical results, 35,561,184 exact sign checks), a reference list and three figures from the app. No result changes.

A scutoid is a cell between two surfaces whose outline changes on the way through: two cells that touched stop touching, and two others start. Slice a four-dimensional polytope with a moving hyperplane: its 3-dimensional cells cross the slice as polygons, and as the hyperplane moves the polygons trade neighbours. Each cell is then a flat-faced scutoid, and the boundary of the polytope a closed scutoid tissue.

Theorem 1. In a generic sweep of a simple 4-polytope the tiling changes only by births, scutoid swaps (the classical 2-2 flip) and deaths, h1, h2 and h3 of them, in every direction. Theorem 1′ gives every dimension (5-cube; 5D permutohedron with the Eulerian numbers; random simple 4-polytopes). Theorem 2: the 120-cell, truncated 120-cell and bitruncated 600-cell sweep with (116, 366, 116), (716, 966, 716) and (716, 2166, 716); Lemma 5: the truncated 600-cell has no pure swap (a rosette tissue). Theorem 4 (balance law): in the bitruncated 600-cell the exchanges between its two kinds of cell balance exactly, 601 each way. Theorem 3: the Swap Rule of close packing (#61) below layer spacing 1/4, with closed forms of its defect on a chamber map, proved by an exact computer-assisted two-parameter computation for every spacing in [1/8, 1/4]; at its walls the holes exchange contacts in symmetric rosette-type events. Section 3: the holes' power cells stacked over the weight are 4-dimensional cells whose 3D slices change neighbours at those walls.

Classical parts credited (the h-vector and its count by a generic height, bistellar flips, the T1 transition as the 2-2 flip). Checked before release by four automated referee passes and one independent attack.

DICTO: ideas, names, constructions and direction. Computation, verification and drafting with Claude (Anthropic).
